content: 1. The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research has issued guidance for the industry on clinical immunogenicity considerations for biosimilar and interchangeable insulin products. This document was accessed on August 29, 2020. 2. Buzzelli et al. (2006) analyzed the impact of generic substitution on pharmaceutical prices and expenditures across OECD countries, publishing their findings in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Finance, Economics, and Policy. 3. Andersson et al. (2007) investigated the effects of a generic substitution reform on the pharmaceutical expenditures of both patients and society, with their study appearing in Health Policy. 4. Clark et al. (2014) evaluated the cost savings and increased adherence associated with an employer value-based benefits program targeting generic antihyperlipidemic and antidiabetic medications, as published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy. 5. Fraeyman et al. (2013) examined the evolution of co-payment structures and generic market share for common medications under Belgium's reference pricing system, with their findings published in Applied Health Economics and Health Policy. 6. Chen et al. (2008) assessed the impact of Taiwan's generic grouping price policy on drug prices and expenditures, focusing on cardiovascular drugs, with their study published in BMC Public Health. 7. Godman et al. (2013) explored the influence of multiple initiatives in Sweden to enhance prescribing efficiency of angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) following the introduction of generic losartan, with implications for other countries, as published in the International Journal of Clinical Practice. 8. Lee et al. (2013) evaluated the success of Argentina's generic drug law, with their findings published in Value in Health. 9. Bhargava et al. (2010) studied the effects of adding generic medication vouchers to a pharmacist academic detailing program on the generic dispensing ratio within a physician-hospital organization, as published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy. 10. Danzon and Furukawa provided cross-national evidence on generic pharmaceuticals, comparing pharmacy-driven and physician-driven markets, as detailed in an NBER Working Paper accessed on August 19, 2020. 11. Balmaceda et al. analyzed the impact of a therapeutic equivalence policy on medicine prices in Chile, with their findings published in Value in Health Regional Issues. 12. Colgan et al. (2015) conducted a systematic review of perceptions of generic medications among the general population, doctors, and pharmacists, with their findings published in BMJ Open. 13. Gebresillassie et al. (2018) evaluated the perceptions and concerns of patients, physicians, and pharmacy professionals regarding generic medicines in Gondar town, Ethiopia, through a cross-sectional survey published in PLoS One. 14. Jacobs et al. (2016) conducted an international cross-sectional survey to assess patient attitudes and understanding of biosimilars, with their findings published in Patient Preference and Adherence. 15. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines on the registration requirements for multisource (generic) pharmaceutical products to establish interchangeability, as part of the WHO Technical Report Series. 16. WHO guidelines on the evaluation of monoclonal antibodies as similar biotherapeutic products (SBPs) were included in the Sixty-Seventh Report of the WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization. 17. WHO guidelines on the quality, safety, and efficacy of biotherapeutic protein products prepared by recombinant DNA technology were updated in the Sixty-Fourth Report of the WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization. 18. Ferraresi et al. (2017) investigated whether centralized purchasing reduces public expenditure, using evidence from the Italian healthcare system, as published in the journal of the Italian Society of Public Economics. 19. Toulemon (2018) analyzed the effect of group purchasing on the prices hospitals pay for medicines, with findings published in Health Economics. 20. Baldi and Vannoni (2017) examined the impact of centralization on pharmaceutical procurement prices, focusing on institutional quality and corruption, as published in Regional Studies. 21. Dubois et al. studied pooled procurement of drugs in lowand middle-income countries, with their findings published in a report accessed on August 21, 2020. 22. Kim and Skordis-Worrall (2017) evaluated whether voluntary pooled procurement could reduce the price of antiretroviral drugs, using efavirenz as a case study, with findings published in Health Policy and Planning. 23. Barbosa and Fiuza (2011) analyzed the effects of demand aggregation and credit risk in pooled procurement, using evidence from Brazilian public purchases of pharmaceuticals and medical supplies, as detailed in a working paper from the São Paulo School of Economics. 24. WHO published a report on multi-country regional pooled procurement of medicines, accessed on August 21, 2020. 25. The Australian Government Department of Health released a fact sheet in 2017 on setting an approved ex-manufacturer price for new or extended pharmaceutical listings. 26. Mamiya provided an update on Japan's drug pricing system in a report accessed on August 29, 2020. 27. Véran proposed Amendment No. 474, which was accessed on August 29, 2020, and is available in French. 28. A report on trade in pharmaceutical products was accessed on August 21, 2020. 29. Bauer analyzed the compounding effect of tariffs on medicines, estimating the real cost of protectionism in emerging markets, as published in the European Centre for International Political Economy. 30. Creese authored a working paper on sales taxes on medicines, accessed on August 29, 2020. 31. The WHO guideline development group included experts from various institutions worldwide, such as the University of Sydney, Fudan University, and the Ministry of Health in Senegal, among others. 32. Declarations of interest from guideline development group members were disclosed, with some members reporting consultancy payments or research funding from pharmaceutical companies. Measures were taken to manage potential conflicts of interest, including recusal from discussions where necessary.
